environmentNotes: Server and client are NOT kept running — start them yourself in the background when a check needs them (server: npm run start:dev from server/, client: bun run dev from client/, http://localhost:5173). This applies on the host; inside a Claude sandbox container (scripts/claude-docker, see docs/knowledgebase/docker-dev-container.md) they are already running — do not start them again. Temp files go in tmp/ (gitignored), never in the project root. The scenarios-* checks (npm run test:scenarios) build and start their own isolated stand (own port, own scn_* schema in DATABASE_URL, needs Postgres and — for mode b — Mailpit, e.g. docker compose -f tests/scenarios/docker-compose.yml up -d); they do not depend on the dev server and never touch it. Iterative runs (finalRun false) are the FAST SET: every `static` check plus `build` — no DB, no stand, no dev app. contract, scenarios-a/b/c, e2e-fast and e2e-full are finalOnly and run only in the final verification. While iterating on behaviour, run just the touched scenario: npm run test:scenarios -- --mode <a|b|c> --only scenarios --grep "<@S-TAG>".

checks.name: build
checks.instructions: Zero compilation errors allowed across all packages. Runs first in the `app` group because it rewrites server/src/public/static/*, which the watched dev backend reloads on — it must never overlap an e2e run.

checks.name: e2e-fast
checks.instructions: Fast @core loop (<3min). Drives the running dev app and the real DB — the `app` group keeps it serial with the build and the other suites.

checks.name: e2e-full
checks.instructions: Full suite — run once right before declaring a work cycle done, not every iteration. Drives the running dev app and the real DB — the `app` group keeps it serial with the build and the other suites.

checks.name: scenarios-a
checks.instructions: Isolated stand in auth mode none: run.mjs builds tmp/scenarios/stand/, starts its own server on a free port in a fresh scn_* schema and drops it afterwards — it does not use or touch the dev server, the dev DB's public schema or server/src/public/static (the run fails if either changed). Exit 2 = preflight (Postgres/Mailpit/Chromium/stray tmp/scenarios/.env.local) — fix the environment, not the tests. The stand build rewrites the installer in place like npm run build, hence the `app` group. Mode A is the big integrated run (~13 min in Oct 2026) and is kept as ONE check on purpose — raise the budget rather than splitting it by --grep, which could silently drop a scenario whose tag no split covers.

checks.name: scenarios-b
checks.instructions: Isolated stand in auth mode password-confirm: run.mjs builds tmp/scenarios/stand/, starts its own server on a free port in a fresh scn_* schema and drops it afterwards — it does not use or touch the dev server, the dev DB's public schema or server/src/public/static (the run fails if either changed). Exit 2 = preflight (Postgres/Mailpit/Chromium/stray tmp/scenarios/.env.local) — fix the environment, not the tests. The stand build rewrites the installer in place like npm run build, hence the `app` group. Each mode is ONE integrated run on purpose: if it outgrows its budget, raise timeoutSeconds rather than splitting it by --grep, which could silently drop a scenario whose tag no split covers.

Exit 2 = preflight (Postgres/Mailpit/Chromium/stray tmp/scenarios/.env.local) — fix the environment, not the tests. The stand build rewrites the installer in place like npm run build, hence the `app` group. Each mode is ONE integrated run on purpose: if it outgrows its budget, raise timeoutSeconds rather than splitting it by --grep, which could silently drop a scenario whose tag no split covers.

checks.name: contract
checks.instructions: Isolated: jest -c jest.contract.config.js boots its own app on a free port in a fresh contract_<uuid> schema (loaded with the world-v1 fixture, dropped afterwards) and never touches the dev server or the dev DB's public schema. Needs only Postgres. It shares Postgres with the server tests and e2e, hence the `app` group. A failing registry row prints its id, route, actor and every response-vs-SQL difference; the meta-test (routes.contract-spec.ts) lists every router route without a row — add the row to server/test/contract/registry/* (see server/test/contract/README.md), never loosen the meta-test. Jest's 'did not exit one second after the test run' warning alone is NOT a failure — judge by the exit code.

checks.name: client-typecheck
checks.instructions: Zero type errors. `vite build` strips types WITHOUT checking them and eslint here is not type-aware, so this is the only check that typechecks the client — never weaken a type or add `any`/`as` to silence it, fix the root cause. Note tsc reports only the first incompatible property of an object literal at a time: after fixing one, re-run, as more may surface behind it.

checks.name: server-typecheck
checks.instructions: Zero type errors. The root build compiles via ncc from server/src/main.ts, so it only ever sees that module graph — this check is the only one covering server/test/** and any file not reachable from main.ts. Never weaken a type or add `any` to silence it, fix the root cause.

checks.name: server-unit
checks.instructions: Only doc-driven algorithm tests (*.algo.spec.ts) plus the migration lock check remain — behaviour is covered by scenarios and contracts, never add other specs. No global setup, no DB, no dev app: pure in-process jest, safe alongside the `app` group.

checks.name: client-unit
checks.instructions: Only doc-driven algorithm tests (*.algo.test.ts) remain — client behaviour is covered by scenarios and tours, never add other client tests. Runs in-process against the sources — it does not touch the DB or the running dev app.

checks.name: tests-typecheck
checks.instructions: Zero type errors. tsc -p tests/tsconfig.json covers tests/e2e, tests/scenarios, tests/golden and playwright.scenarios.config.ts — Playwright strips types without checking them, so this is the only check that typechecks the browser suites. Never weaken a type or add `any`/`as` to silence it, fix the root cause.

checks.name: scripts-unit
checks.instructions: Node's built-in test runner over scripts/__tests__/*.test.js and client/scripts/__tests__/*.test.cjs. Pure helper coverage for the build/release scripts — it never shells out to docker, never touches the DB and never touches the running dev app.

checks.name: hook-tests
checks.instructions: Only doc-driven algorithm tests (*.algo.test.js) remain in hook/.claude/telemetry_tool/__tests__ (rows owned by the server side are skipped by design) — hook behaviour is covered by tests/scenarios/hook. The file list is collected by hook/scripts/run-tests.js. Needs neither the dev server nor the DB.
